spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The mathematical work is the preservation of a finite factorization after passage to the limiting law. The ordinary characteristic function remains an absolutely convergent product of single-factor transforms, while the derivative-weighted transform becomes a convergent sum of products with one or two marked factors; the separate summability conditions are exactly what keeps those markings controlled.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source obtains the limiting transform A(y;μ) as an infinite product of K_0(y,r_k). For the weighted measure ν it passes from the finite expansion to infinite one- and two-index sums whose terms contain K_1 or K_2 insertions among K_0 factors. Absolute convergence follows from the previously stated S_0, S_1, and S_2 conditions, and the remaining finite-to-infinite discrepancy is a tail product tending to 1.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a closure step: independence gives an algebraic decomposition at finite level, and summability certifies that the same decomposition survives completion. The weighted law is not merely another product; its marks record where the derivative weight enters and expose the extra proof burden created by that weight.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Fourier representation converts addition of independent circular contributions into multiplication, while marked factors encode differentiated or weighted contributions without expanding the full distribution in physical space. The resulting product-series representation is the bridge to later frequency-decay and inversion arguments.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The unweighted product only uses the base summability, whereas the weighted expansion needs both first- and second-order coefficient sums. Without absolute convergence, neither the infinite marked sums nor the removal of the tail product is justified.
directed.uncertainty: The OCR damages several summation indices and K-factor labels, so their exact placement should be checked against the scan. The product-limit mechanism and the stated absolute-convergence dependencies are explicit.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The key move is to split the phase sum into a fixed head and a small random tail, then turn concentration of the tail into spatial decay of the full density by convolution. Linearizing the tail gives exponential-moment control, and the weighted case is recovered through a second tail measure and a Schwarz estimate rather than by silently treating it as an ordinary probability law.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Writing f_n=f_q+f_{q,n}, Fubini gives μ_n(E)=∫μ_q(E-u)dμ_{q,n}(u) and hence F_n(x)=∫F_q(x-u)dμ_{q,n}(u). The nonlinear tail is compared with its linear part; Parseval estimates moments of that linear sum and yields exponentially small translated-tail probabilities. Bounded head densities and differentiation under the convolution then give Gaussian-type majorants for F_n, F, and their derivatives. For G_n the source proves an inequality involving F_q and a weighted tail measure ν_{q,n}, with ν_{q,n}(E) bounded by a constant times μ_{q,n}(E)^{1/2}.
directed.conceptual_reading: This proof localizes two tasks: the head supplies regularity, while the tail supplies localization. It shows that a density can inherit strong pointwise decay from concentration of an otherwise implicit tail distribution, and that the same architecture survives weighting only after an additional moment comparison.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The head-tail convolution is the bridge from probabilistic tail bounds to analytic estimates on densities. Translation of a bounded head support converts a distant evaluation point into a rare tail event; differentiating the fixed head factor transfers the identical bound to derivatives.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The argument needs q large enough for the analytic linearization error and exponential moment estimate, as well as the relevant convergent coefficient sums. The weighted result additionally uses control of the derivative tail and Schwarz; it is not a consequence of the unweighted convolution formula alone.
directed.uncertainty: Several constants and displayed exponents are OCR-degraded. The source clearly supports Gaussian-type spatial majorants and the head-tail mechanism, but the exact numerical exponent and constants should be scan-verified before reuse.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Strict positivity is obtained from reachability plus residual randomness, not from smoothness. Divergence of the radii lets a finite block of sufficiently small phase vectors close a polygon to any desired displacement, while the remaining tail has positive probability of staying near zero; convolution then turns positive mass in every open set into pointwise positivity of the limiting density.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source first contrasts the summable-radius case, where all values stay in a bounded set, with the divergent-radius case. A second-moment estimate shows that a sufficiently remote tail lies in a small circle with uniformly positive probability. Using l(z)≈l_1z for small z and divergence of ∑r_k, phases in a finite tail block can be chosen so its vector sum reaches the displacement from a fixed head value to an arbitrary target. Thus the limiting measure is positive on every set with interior. The limiting convolution F(x)=∫F_q(x-u)dQ_q(u), with Q_q positive on open sets, then gives F(x)>0 everywhere.
directed.conceptual_reading: Full support is constructed geometrically before it is upgraded analytically to strict density positivity. The proof separates controllability of a finite phase block from robustness supplied by unused tail variables.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The polygonal vector-sum picture translates phase freedom into reachability in the value plane. Convolution with a smooth positive head density bridges open-set support of the tail law to pointwise positivity of F.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Divergence of ∑r_k and the locally nonzero linear term of l are essential. If the radii are summable, the support is bounded. This span proves positivity for the unweighted density F; positivity of the derivative-weighted density G requires the distinct nondegeneracy argument that follows.
directed.uncertainty: OCR obscures some circle radii and numerical probability bounds, but the phase-selection, open-set support, and convolution implications are readable.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The weighted positivity problem is solved by finding redundancy in the phase-to-value map: the same head value has two regular phase representations whose derivative weights differ. Two inverse charts and a uniform separation of those weights prevent the squared weight from cancelling after an arbitrary tail contribution, so positivity of an unweighted tail density can be transferred to G.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: After permuting two sufficiently small unequal radii to the front, the source constructs two phase pairs with f_2(θ_1,θ_2) equal, g_2 different, and nonzero Jacobian for the map from phases to the two real coordinates of f_2. Convexity of the small image curves produces two transverse intersections; proportional and nonproportional cases for the analytic functions are treated separately to ensure the g_2 values differ. Local inverse maps on two phase neighborhoods have Jacobians bounded below, and the corresponding head weights remain separated. Fubini and change of variables then lower-bound ν_n(E) by a positive constant times an unweighted tail measure averaged over a value neighborhood. Passing to the limit and using positivity of the tail density yields G(x)>0 for every x.
directed.conceptual_reading: A weighted pushforward may vanish even when its unweighted support is full. The additional resource is a nondegenerate fiber with two representations carrying separated weights; fiber redundancy converts a possible cancellation or degeneracy into a uniform lower bound.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The phase-to-value map, its Jacobian, and two local inverse charts are the operative intermediate objects. They bridge geometric multiplicity of representations to a measure lower bound, which convolution with the already-positive tail density turns into global positivity.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The mechanism uses small analytic circular components, unequal radii, regular preimages, and the divergent-radius tail positivity proved earlier. It is not a general theorem that every derivative-weighted pushforward of a full-support law is positive.
directed.uncertainty: The OCR is unreliable for exact Jacobian notation, constants, and the displayed proportionality formulas. The two-preimage, weight-separation, change-of-variables mechanism is nevertheless explicit.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The rate at which component radii shrink is converted into a regularity scale. Assigning successively smaller factors to a large frequency forces the characteristic-function products to decay exponentially; a geometric rate gives a fixed exponential type and real analyticity, while supergeometric decay gives every exponential rate and hence entire extension.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The proof starts from the product representations for A(y;μ) and A(y;ν). With b defined by the limsup geometric rate of r_n, any a>b eventually bounds r_n by a^n. The local bound for K_0 supplies roughly one inverse-frequency contribution per allocated small factor; multiplying these bounds and using Stirling produces O(e^{-c|y|}) decay for the products, with a corresponding polynomial prefactor absorbed in the weighted sums. If b=0, c can be taken arbitrarily large. Fourier inversion then yields real analyticity in the first case and an entire function of the two real-coordinate variables in the second.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a quantitative refinement of the earlier smoothness argument: factor abundance controls polynomial decay, but factor scale controls exponential decay. The asymptotic geometry of the radius sequence therefore becomes the analytic continuation budget of the density.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge runs from radius decay to factorwise Fourier decay, from the product to global exponential frequency decay, and then through Fourier inversion to spatial analyticity or entire extension.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The conclusion depends on the explicit product and marked-product formulas and their summability; a qualitative statement r_n→0 alone only supports smoothness, not analyticity. The weighted transform must absorb its marked-factor polynomial growth.
directed.uncertainty: The OCR corrupts the exact hypothesis as printed and several constants in the limsup estimate. The geometric-versus-supergeometric dichotomy and its Fourier-decay proof are explicit and agree with the bounded dossier.

unit_result_entry.why_material: When the square-sum diverges at a boundary parameter while remaining convergent inside, the characteristic function tends to zero away from frequency zero under an integrable uniform majorant, so Fourier inversion and dominated convergence give uniform vanishing of the density and its derivatives.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: This is the later source of the Re(s)→1/2 boundary behavior.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: At the boundary, diverging quadratic mass flattens the density rather than producing a pointwise limiting profile. Away from zero frequency, more small factors force the characteristic function to zero; a uniform integrable Fourier majorant then turns that punctured-frequency collapse into uniform vanishing of the density and every derivative.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Theorem 10 assumes r_k(a) are continuous, tend to zero uniformly, and the relevant sums converge for interior parameters while S_0 diverges at the boundary a_1. A parameter-independent integrable majorant for |y|^p|A(y;μ_a)| is inherited from the preceding uniform estimates. On each annulus 0<c≤|y|≤C, the product formula and a small-factor bound of the form |K_0(y,r_k)|≤1-c' r_k^2|y|^2 force A(y;μ_a)→0 as a→a_1 because S_0 diverges. Dominated Fourier inversion gives uniform convergence of F_a and each partial derivative to zero.
directed.conceptual_reading: The law does not lose total mass; its mass spreads so broadly that every fixed spatial location sees vanishing density. The proof isolates the exceptional zero frequency, where characteristic functions remain normalized, from the positive-measure frequency region that controls inversion.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The infinite product converts variance divergence into characteristic-function collapse on punctured annuli. Dominated convergence in Fourier space is the bridge from that collapse to uniform spatial flattening, including after multiplication by frequency monomials for derivatives.
directed.boundary_or_failure: There is no claim that the measures themselves converge to the zero measure, and convergence cannot hold at y=0. The displayed theorem concerns the unweighted density F; extending it to a weighted law would require separately stated domination.
directed.uncertainty: The OCR damages the boundary value and some product constants. The dossier identifies this boundary with the later real-part one-half limit, and the dominated-convergence mechanism is explicit.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The abstract torus theory is instantiated by a precise dictionary: logarithm turns each Euler factor into the analytic component l(z)=-log(1-z), differentiation supplies m(z)=z/(1-z) and a log-prime weight, and prime powers set the radii. Verifying the three coefficient sums and radius rates imports smoothness, positivity, entire extension, parameter stability, decay, and boundary flattening without rebuilding those arguments for Euler products.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For the partial Euler product, the source writes log ζ_n as a sum of -log(1-p_k^{-s}e^{2πiθ_k}) and its s-derivative using the corresponding rational factor and log p_k. It identifies these with the abstract f_n and g_n by taking l(z)=-log(1-z), m(z)=zl'(z)=z/(1-z), r_k=p_k^{-a}, and λ_k=-log p_k. The hypotheses of Theorems 5–10 are then checked in their respective ranges. Theorem 11 concludes finite and limiting absolute continuity, arbitrary smoothness in the interior half-plane, strict positivity in the stated strip, entire dependence on the two value coordinates in the narrower strip, joint parameter regularity, uniform convergence and Gaussian-type decay, symmetry under conjugation, and uniform boundary vanishing for the log-density.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is theorem reuse by structural matching. The logarithmic Euler product is recognized as an independent-phase analytic series, so arithmetic input is compressed into the sequences of radii and log-prime weights whose convergence properties select the available analytic conclusions.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Taking logarithms is the decisive representation change: a multiplicative Euler product becomes an additive torus sum to which convolution and Fourier-product methods apply. The prime-local dictionary bridges the abstract component model to log-Euler-product value and derivative-weighted distributions.
directed.boundary_or_failure: These are torus distributions for finite and limiting Euler-product models. Their identification with actual vertical distributions of log zeta still needs the prime-log equidistribution and limiting transfer developed later. Pointwise boundary flattening of a density is not disappearance of probability mass.
directed.uncertainty: OCR renders one-half as 89 and damages some prime exponents and finite thresholds. The choices of l, m, radii, and log-prime weights, as well as the qualitative theorem conclusions, are clear.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Exponentiation is treated as a many-to-one pushforward rather than a harmless change of variables. Each nonzero value has all logarithmic lifts, so its density is a periodized sum over those lifts with the appropriate Jacobian; strong decay in the log plane makes the infinite sum differentiable termwise, while the origin remains a distinguished boundary point.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source maps the log-value measures through exp. For a Borel set E it gives μ^{val}(E)=μ^{log}(log E), while the derivative-weighted measure includes the factor e^{2ξ_1} on log E. For x≠0, the ordinary density is |x|^{-2} times the sum of the log-density over all values of log x; the derivative-weighted density is the corresponding sum of weighted log-densities, with cancellation of the Jacobian factor. Both are defined to be zero at x=0. Gaussian bounds in the log plane uniformly dominate the 2πi-periodized series and all differentiated series, yielding smoothness, positivity away from zero, parameter continuity, uniform convergence, and analytic or entire statements after composition with exp. The final boundary assertion retains explicit powers of |x|.
directed.conceptual_reading: Exponentiation quotients the log plane by vertical period and collapses its far-left end to zero. Regularity transfers through this quotient only after accounting for multiplicity and Jacobian, and the weighted law transforms differently because its derivative weight compensates that Jacobian.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The covering-space picture log x+2πih is the useful bridge object. Periodization transports log-value densities to the punctured value plane, while decay of distant lifts controls the infinite preimage sum and its derivatives.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The formulas are singular at x=0 and positivity is asserted only away from zero. The source explicitly warns that boundary vanishing is false if the prescribed |x| powers are omitted; even bounded-set mass need not vanish. Thus unweighted uniform boundary conclusions cannot be imported from the log plane.
directed.uncertainty: Some density symbols and exponents are OCR-damaged, but equations 77–82 clearly support the pushforward, lift-sum, and Jacobian structure. Exact derivative-weight powers should be checked against the scan.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Partial Euler products first supply ordinary almost-periodic objects whose torus laws are exact by equidistribution, then generalized convergence theorems transfer their Jensen functions and distributions to zeta and log zeta.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The transfer is conditional on the stated mean convergence and branch-domain hypotheses and does not extend automatically beyond Re(s)>1/2.
related_synthesis_entries.title: Finite Euler products form a two-stage transfer scaffold

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The abstract independent phases are connected to one deterministic vertical trajectory by rational independence of the log primes. Long-time averaging of any continuous torus observable equals Haar averaging, so the previously constructed torus measures become exact asymptotic value laws for finite Euler products, including the derivative-weighted law.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The partial Euler product and its logarithm along s=a+it are written as torus functions evaluated at phases λ_kt, with λ_k proportional to -log p_k. Linear independence of these frequencies gives M_t H(λ_1t,…,λ_nt)=∫H dm for every continuous H on the finite torus. Applying this to exponential test functions identifies the Fourier transforms, hence the torus measures μ_{n,a} and ν_{n,a}, with the ordinary and derivative-weighted vertical asymptotic distributions of log ζ_n. The source then expresses the finite-product Jensen function as the logarithmic potential of μ_{n,a} and identifies its second derivative with 2π times the weighted density.
directed.conceptual_reading: A one-parameter deterministic motion emulates independent phase sampling because its orbit is equidistributed. This supplies the missing semantic justification for treating prime phases as independent in finite vertical-value statistics.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The dense torus flow t↦(λ_1t,…,λ_nt) is the bridge between vertical motion and Haar phase space. Characteristic functions make equality of the two averaging procedures into equality of distributions, and logarithmic potentials then connect those laws to Jensen curvature.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The equidistribution statement directly handles finite partial products and continuous torus observables. Passing to log zeta or zeta requires the separate convergence theorems and branch-domain hypotheses; finite-dimensional equidistribution alone does not justify the infinite limit.
directed.uncertainty: Exact normalization constants in the frequencies and Fourier formulas are OCR-degraded. Linear independence, Haar averaging, distribution identification, and the finite Jensen-curvature consequence are explicit.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The weighted log-value density becomes a local curvature density for a global Jensen function. Once the log-zeta value law is identified, its logarithmic potential is twice differentiable in the vertical-line parameter; integrating that curvature recovers mean motions and strip zero frequencies, so value statistics are converted into zero-counting information.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: For each a>1/2, Theorem 13 gives an asymptotic distribution μ_a for log ζ(a+it). It represents the Jensen function of log ζ(s)-x as ∫log|u-x|dμ_a(u)=∫log|u-x|F_a(u)du and states that its second derivative in a is 2πG_a(x), where G_a is the derivative-weighted log-value density. The left and right mean motions equal the first derivative of this Jensen function, and the relative frequency of zeros in a strip is the difference of those slopes divided by 2π, equivalently the integral of G_a(x) across the strip. The Jensen function diverges as a approaches 1/2 from the right, and conjugation supplies the negative-height version.
directed.conceptual_reading: The theorem factors zero counting into a potential-theoretic chain: value distribution gives a logarithmic potential, derivative weighting gives its curvature, and integration of curvature gives argument motion and zero frequency. G_a is therefore not decorative auxiliary data but the local density of Jensen convexity.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The logarithmic potential of the asymptotic value measure is the intermediate representation linking two-dimensional value statistics to one-dimensional variation in real part. Jensen theory then bridges its slope changes to zeros in vertical strips.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The statements apply in the half-plane a>1/2 and, for log zeta, within the specified branch domain. Boundary divergence and unbounded zero frequencies do not locate zeros on the critical line and do not prove the Riemann hypothesis. The transfer relies on the earlier finite-product convergence and density regularity.
directed.uncertainty: OCR damages branch notation, large-a exceptional formulas, and some normalizations. The 2π curvature relation, strip integral, boundary divergence, and negative-height symmetry are readable.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The log-zeta curvature theorem is transported to zeta values through all logarithmic lifts of the target. The periodized pushforward explains both the parallel Jensen and zero-frequency formulas and the exceptional roles of target values zero and one; exponentiation preserves the architecture but not every boundary statement unchanged.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Theorem 14 states that ζ(a+it) has the asymptotic value distribution μ̃_a for a>1/2. The Jensen function of ζ(s)-x is its logarithmic potential and has second derivative 2πG̃_a(x), with mean motions given by its first derivative and strip zero frequencies by the integral of G̃_a(x). The proof first establishes the analogous formulas for finite Euler products, then passes to the limit using Theorem 12. It also relates the zeta Jensen quantity to the family of log-zeta quantities over all logarithms of x, using a convergent majorant to integrate the resulting series. For x≠0 the Jensen function diverges as a approaches 1/2; for x=0 it is identically zero, and x=1 has a separate large-real-part formula. Conjugation again gives negative-height limits.
directed.conceptual_reading: A many-sheeted representation can transfer a theorem only after summing over every lift and tracking exceptional fibers. The zeta result is thus a synthesis of the log-plane curvature laws rather than a formally identical copy.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Exponentiation and the set of logarithmic preimages of x bridge log-zeta value laws to zeta value laws. The logarithmic-potential identity and its twice-differentiated form carry curvature, mean motion, and zero frequency through that bridge.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The boundary divergence excludes x=0, and the large-real-part behavior distinguishes x=1. All conclusions concern a>1/2 and value equations ζ(s)=x; they do not assert where ordinary zeta zeros lie on or relative to the critical line.
directed.uncertainty: OCR obscures several exact formulas and exceptional-case constants, but the asymptotic distribution, potential, 2π curvature, lift-sum proof, and stated exceptions are clear.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The final corollary converts boundary growth of the preceding Jensen slopes into a global abundance statement: when the whole half-plane to the right of one-half is allowed, the zero count grows faster than any fixed linear normalization. It is a cumulative consequence of strip-frequency formulas, not a new localization theorem.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Theorem 15 states that N(T)/T→∞ when N(T) counts either zeros of log ζ(s)-x in the relevant branch portion of Re(s)>1/2 for arbitrary x, or zeros of ζ(s)-x in Re(s)>1/2 for nonzero x. It is presented as a corollary of Theorems 13 and 14.
directed.conceptual_reading: Finite-strip densities of zeros are accumulated while the left boundary approaches the variance-divergent edge. The unbounded normalized total records growth of the integrated Jensen curvature across the entire open half-plane.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is the preceding identity between strip zero frequency and the integral of the derivative-weighted value density. Boundary divergence lets those finite-strip frequencies become unbounded as strips exhaust Re(s)>1/2.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This is not a Riemann-hypothesis statement, does not place zeros on Re(s)=1/2, and does not say that every fixed strip has infinite normalized frequency. The zeta-minus-value statement excludes x=0, while the log-zeta statement retains its branch-domain restriction.
directed.uncertainty: The span is short and delegates its proof to Theorems 13 and 14. The half-plane symbol is OCR-degraded, but the dossier and surrounding theorem statements identify it as Re(s)>1/2.
